body: **Stack:** Rust 1.98.1 pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml` (edition 2024, `rust-version` 1.96), one Cargo workspace (`crates/*`, the `fuzz/` workspace excluded) building one native `viola` binary: std threads with Tokio only inside `viola-mcp`, clap `=4.6.7`, portable-pty `=0.9.0` behind viola's own PTY seam, vt100 `=0.16.2` for readiness, interprocess `=2.4.4` local sockets carrying JSON-RPC 2.0 over ndjson, ndjson append logs and atomic JSON snapshots (no database, broker, container or hosting), rmcp 3.4.1 (`>=3.4.1, <3.5`) for the stdio MCP server; CI on GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` against the fake agent; deployed by a local `cargo install`, the plugin embedded and loaded with `--plugin-dir`.
- **Test runner:** cargo-nextest (process-per-test, JUnit, `retries = 0`) + `cargo test --doc`; nextest is the runner, and a plain `cargo test` run (`cargo test --bin viola`) is not supported

- **Fake agent:** `viola-fake-agent` (root `[[bin]]`, feature `fake-agent`) replays `fixtures/claude/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json` (the spine, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants and the `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants and the `SessionStart.resume-1.json` resume variant recorded by `viola verify`, the dialog tier by its Runs C and D, the framing tier by Run B's added pastes, the resume variant by Run E; `2.1.287`'s relayed dialog fixtures superseded and kept, `RELAYED.md`), runs absolute exec-form hooks from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (a group's `matcher` evaluated against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name`), gates script steps on `--control`, and writes an ndjson `--receipt`; its argv-only `--transcript` creates `<exe dir>/transcripts/` at 0700 at start and gives the launch SessionStart a `transcript_path` to a seeded 0600 file named by its session id (replayed framing variants not rewritten), and every stamping `viola verify` against it (harness `boot` and the stamped-home helpers) passes it `--transcript` beside `--framing` (the framing-free verify helper passes none), and every test-started `viola verify`, `viola run` and `viola revive` and every harness boot stamping runs under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only, never the runner's real `HOME` (the harness's supervised wrappers of a stamped session too, under a session user home seeded with an empty config), the fake agent told that config file by `--trust-config` (a `--record` verify keeps the real `HOME` and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead); its print mode `-p/--print <prompt>` fires the spine fixtures, prints `ok` and exits 0, `--trust-config <file>` reads trust from that config file by the CLI's walk (the canonical cwd's exact key then each parent up to the git root, so inside a repository the cwd's own record counts, through a bounded read; any failure reads untrusted), `--screens` / `--trusted-root` / `--turn-stop` write `Screen.modal|ready|turn` (under `--screens` with an untrusted cwd it draws claude 2.1.325's unnumbered trust form over the set's recorded modal, the selector first on No; arrows move the selector, Enter on No exits 1, and SessionStart fires only after Enter on the trust row, which draws the ready screen), `--dialogs` replays a pasted dialog prompt's recorded variants in claim order, and `--framing` replays Run B's recorded paste, `/compact` and `/clear` variants (the probed `/compact` its recorded `SessionStart.compact-1` with the last fired SessionStart's `session_id`; the exact verify echo probe command, like a stdout-tag local command under `--local-command-mode`, one stdout tag line appended to the last started session's transcript and no hook fired) for verify's six interactive runs (two capped test-only holds: `--stop-receipt-hold-ms`, 1 s, holds the Stop receipt for a race test; `--paste-hint-ms`, 10 s, holds a cleared screen after the long paste's turn; the test-only hold `--trust-record-blank` makes a start trusted by the trust record alone draw no screen, holding verify's Run F window open for a stop case; and the test-only screen switches `--tag-turn-screen <phase>` and `--long-turn-screen <phase>` draw the named screen after the tag-like paste's turn alone and after the long paste's turn alone; under `--screens` a trusted start given `--start-screen <phase>` draws `Screen.<phase>` in place of its ready screen and keeps it standing, each stdin byte one key receipt line, Ctrl-C ending it with no key line, and no byte reaching the input box) (what `viola verify` drives: `tests/cli_verify.rs` pins verify's lines by literal asserts); CI stamps homes only by running `viola verify` against it at the recorded `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs`) (the root `stamped_home`, each stamped test home a copy, never a link, of one `viola verify` stamp taken per pair of built binaries, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes and taken under an exclusive lock, and harness `boot` step 4, unless `--unstamped`; `StampedHome::unstamped` for the unverified-path tests; `SessionOptions::unstamped`, default false, the in-test form of `boot --unstamped` for a harness session); the real `claude` never runs in CI — only the local `run --local-live`, refused under `CI` (`live-in-ci`), and the live starts of the one standing test-only rig `viola-live-rig` in viola-e2e, run by hand under the founder's start cap for each chunk, each ledgered with its clock time first, its live arm refused under CI and its rehearsals over the fake agent run in CI — and neither does the real `hyprctl`, which the same fake agent stands in for as `hyprctl` by its own file name in a test-scoped bin dir, reading its mode and reply set from files beside its exe, except in viola-hyprland's own unit tests, which serve `hyprctl` by a planted shell stub because cargo-mutants runs only the mutated package's tests, so a root-package test cannot kill that crate's mutants. The committed `fixtures/claude/*/*.json` (the recorded sets, each with its dialog, framing and resume variants and its agents fixture `Agents.recorded-1.json`, Run B's own row of its one `claude agents --json` read, where it holds them, and 2.1.287's superseded relayed fixtures included; the stamped sets are the `STAMPED` literal of `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`, each stamped at every relied row on every build, the drift-only sets its `DRIFT_ONLY`) are walked for hygiene by a run-time directory walk against `schemas/claude-fixture.v1.json`, the `Agents.*.json` agents fixtures against `schemas/claude-agents-fixture.v1.json` (`agents_fixtures_pass_hygiene`), the `Mcp.*.json` MCP exchanges (recorded by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap`) left out of that walk and walked by `mcp_fixtures` against `schemas/claude-mcp-fixture.v1.json` (`mcp_fixtures_pass_hygiene`), then replayed against `viola mcp` by `mcp_recorded_exchange` (the served `tools/list` result holding the recorded key and type shape and tool names in order), the `Screen.*.json` screens apart against `schemas/claude-screen.v1.json` (email and row-seam usernames refused too, and a box prompt row with text after the prompt char or a box rule row with any other text: a box row is recorded as its literal alone, `planted_box_row_beyond_its_literal_is_rejected`) (rstest 0.27 `#[files]` refuses an empty glob at compile time); the same walk drives the drift contract `contract_fake_agent_drift`, which compares each print-mode hook's receipt `stdin_hex` byte for byte with the recorded fixture and the hook order with the spine literal, and replays every dialog variant and every framing variant byte for byte, and replays the resume variant (`fake_agent_resume_replay_matches_every_recorded_resume_set`) and, once resumed into its own session, the compact variant (`fake_agent_compact_replay_matches_every_recorded_compact_set`), and compares the key and type shape of the fake agent's `agents` rows with each recorded `Agents.*.json` set (`fake_agent_agents_replay_matches_every_recorded_agents_set`) (the resume launch: under `--resume <id>`, one of its argv options (`--settings <file>` accepted, its value consumed and ignored; beside the options the mode word `agents`, a first word `agents` answering `agents --json` from files beside its exe (`agents-mode`, `agents-rows.json` and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry), built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`, with no option and no env added), the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it (recorded by Run E since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows), else its recorded default (a set without the variant), with `source` `resume` and that `session_id`, or with `--fork-session` the compiled fork id; the `--resume` shape is the `resume-session` ledger row) ; the committed Hyprland fixtures (recorded only by the test-only `viola-hypr-tap`, under the same scrub) are walked for hygiene and against their schema too, each Hyprland reply held to its closed per-request string keep-list — no insta snapshot

- **Path 5 — the wheel** — human key → `human-typing` (exit 10) (the stdin classifier's closed non-editing list is unit-pinned in `src/run/wheel.rs`: its reply strings whole and split, and negative controls that stay typing; its reading on a real terminal is a local live measurement, foot 1.28.0 at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive), `pause` → `manual-pause`, `release` back, `release` with `from` → exit 20, harness turns never flip it but a `send` during one is refused `turn-running` (exit 13, nothing typed) until its `turn-ended`; a turn left running under a driver-held wheel is cleared by `pause` then `release`, never by a bare `release`; as landed `tests/tui_wheel.rs` + `tests/cli_wheel.rs` in CI on `ubuntu-latest`, the MCP `send` step and its refusal checks landed at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs` `mcp_tools_path4_path5_answer_by_id_and_a_paused_send`; no MCP result, body or tool description names `release`)

| Mutation | 0 missed beyond the host-excluded mutants the harness leaves out, 0 timeout, unviable ≤ caught at a `run --mutants` (the epoch-boundary audit, or on demand); one known survivor stands against the `missed` rule: a mutant replacing a client seam's `peer_admitted` read (`src/cmd/client.rs` `connect`, `src/cmd/hook.rs` `connect`, `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` `frame`) with an always-admit survives every committed test by construction, one account making no foreign peer and no seam allowed, and it stands as version 0.1.0's known limit, read at each epoch-boundary audit (matrix#v1-44) | cargo-mutants `--in-diff`; more unviable than caught mutants is red (`unviable-exceeds-caught`: the builds failed, nothing was tested); a Rust delta reads a fresh `outcomes.json` (`verdict:"counted"`), a diff with no `.rs` path passes as `verdict:"no-rust-delta"`, and one whose `.rs` paths are all test targets (`tests/`, `benches/`, `examples/`) as `verdict:"test-only-rust-delta"` (cargo-mutants mutates none of them); a mixed diff is `counted`; `--file <path>` is the scoped inner loop (`verdict:"scoped"`); `--package <member>` scores one whole member, the boundary tier's form (`verdict:"package"`, viola-e2e included); a mutant the host cannot compile or reach is "not measured here; owed to {route entry}" by coordinate, never "equivalent", and `missed == 0` reads over the measurable set; the harness applies the first case itself: a missed mutant whose whole span sits under a `cfg` attribute proved false for the host leaves `survived` and `failures` and is named in the document's `mutants.host_excluded` (`{name, cfg}`, absent when empty; `tested` still counts it), while a const-gated mutant stays a record by coordinate and cargo-mutants' own lines still say MISSED (the first whole-member viola-e2e score on the Linux dev host: 718 mutants in 5356 s, 656 caught, 2 missed, 0 timeout, 60 unviable, the 2 missed in `prepare` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs`, deleted with the Windows scratch wipe and recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`), both read killed on the Linux dev host by its scratch case at chunk 2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii; chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup-ii; both read caught on `windows-2025` in run 38036448183, chunk 2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade; the Epoch 4 boundary audit's Linux whole-member runs read 47 missed, disposed: 29 by a nextest case in the owning package at chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors, the 2 `prepare` rows as recorded (read killed on the Linux dev host), and the 16 in `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` (whose code now sits under its children in `src/cmd/verify/typed/`) by a case in its unit tests after a behaviour-preserving restatement at chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii, none owed; the Epoch 5 boundary audit's own run is the reader that confirms the 45 kills; the Epoch 5 boundary audit's 16 survivors were each disposed by a nextest case in the package that owns the mutated file, 10 killed and 6 after a behaviour-preserving restatement, none equivalent or recorded, at chunk 2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii). On the Linux dev host every mutation run takes a NOCOW btrfs `TMPDIR` (`<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch`). Each run's `outcomes.json` and JUnit are archived in `target/run-archive/<n>`. No chunk, pre-push or CI mutation gate since 2026-09-28: `run --mutants` is named-only, and `/andromeda-code-audit` runs mutation at the epoch boundary, with no Windows leg (`windows-mutants.yml` and the `cfg(windows)` code out of the tree, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`); the `mutants` nextest profile is `terminate = "wait"`; the two real-cargo-mutants harness self-tests run ungated, never `#[ignore]` |

| Performance budget | hook `max` < `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` (1.0 s), the constant `gate.rs` `perf()` imports (SessionEnd and the spine hooks; the hook's own connect deadline is the provisional 750 ms `CONNECT_DEADLINE`, asserted below it) | hyperfine `-N --warmup 3 --runs 30` via `run --perf` (its rows, `pre-tool-use` included, on an unstamped perf session), gated on `max` by `gate --require perf` in the `perf` job; the fail-open matrix also asserts `< 1.0 s` per case |

- `cargo install --locked cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1 cargo-mutants cargo-deny@0.20.2` — test / coverage / mutation / policy tools, each at the version `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins (CI uses taiki-e/install-action, SHA-pinned)

- `cargo install --locked hyperfine cargo-modules zizmor@1.30.1` (hyperfine and cargo-modules at the versions `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins) — perf gate, orphans gate + on-demand boundary review, workflow lint (CI installs cargo-modules this way in `lint`: taiki-e has no manifest for it)

- `viola verify [--record <dir>] [-- <program> [args…]]` — drive one print-mode probe (Haiku) and six interactive PTY runs (Run A untrusted in an OS-temp dir, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` with seven compiled pastes (the probe prompt, a long text, a tag-like text, a text holding one inner LF, `/compact`, `/clear`, then `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent`, the local-command-echo row's probe, skipped with that row failed when no transcript is readable) and one `claude agents --json` read once its first turn has settled, before the added pastes (held in memory, spawn pair `agents-probe`, no start added; in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it), Run C's dialogs in `-dialogs/`, Run D's plan in `-plan/`, then Run E in `-resume/` resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>` (input empty, no `--settings`), then Run F in an untrusted temp folder whose trust record verify writes into the Claude config file its child reads (never creating an absent file; a run or revive start writes a record only for its own untrusted spawn folder, on a verified CLI), passing the trust-record row only when the record was written, Run A showed the trust modal and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box; no key into any dialog — the probe hook answers C and D's) against the CLI (default `claude`), check the relied ledger rows (`LedgerRow::relied()`, on every build), print `[NN/MM]` step lines ending `pass`, `absent` or `fail` (`absent` on the browser-tools-prompt row alone, when no run met the CLI's browser-tools prompt; `MM` the relied count; the last `[MM/MM] browser-tools-prompt …`) + the `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail` summary on stdout (`<n>` counting every relied row that counts toward verified, an absent browser-tools-prompt among them) and write `ledger/stamps.json`; exit 1 on a failing row; exit 1 with the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, no step line, no summary and no log line when `check_home_tree` refuses its home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens (and the same pair, exit 1, after the step lines, when `update_stamps` refuses `ledger/stamps.json`, with `detail:"strict-modes-failed"` on its `process-exit` under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`); a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM kills its child with no key, removes only the probe dirs it created and its own trust record from the Claude config file, writes no stamp, leaves stdout empty, prints `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI` and exits 1 (SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install leaves the dirs to remove by hand). `--record <dir>` also writes the scrubbed `<dir>/<ver>/<Event>.default.json` fixtures, the `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` dialog variants, Run B's `paste-<n>` / `compact-<n>` / `clear-<n>` framing variants, Run E's first SessionStart as `SessionStart.resume-1.json`, Run B's agents read as `Agents.recorded-1.json` (Run B's own row only) and signature-only `Screen.<phase>.json` screens (a footer or modal row whole, the input box's rule row as its rule chars alone and its prompt row as the prompt char alone, every other row empty; a box whose live prompt row holds a home path, the username or an email refuses the recording) when 0 rows fail; an unclean recording is refused naming the file and check code. A hidden `--record-first-screens`, absent from `--help` and passed only by the live rig, makes a failed `--record` verify write a first-screen file of whole scrubbed rows per run short of the input box (Run A's trust excepted), refused whole when unclean, kept locally and never committed. Run it from a folder you trust in Claude Code whose external CLAUDE.md import is answered. Against the real CLI: local only, spends tokens; CI runs it only against the fake agent's `-p/--print` mode and its `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root --dialogs --framing --transcript --trust-config` interactive modes, under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only and named to the fake agent by `--trust-config` (every stamping verify passes `--transcript` beside `--framing`, or Run B's echo probe is skipped and the local-command-echo row fails). The `Mcp.<variant>.json` MCP exchanges are recorded not by `--record` but by the test-only `viola-mcp-tap` (`record` / `fixture`, the same scrub and closed refusal codes; architecture §Occupied Resources → Binary); the recorded Hyprland replies likewise by the test-only `viola-hypr-tap`, under the same scrub

- Stamps file: `ledger/stamps.json` in the Ledger stamps envelope `{"v":1,"written_at","writer":"verify","data":{"versions":{"<ver>":{"verified_at","rows":{…},"measured":{…}}}}}` (arch §Standard Contracts); a version is verified only when its stamp holds every relied row (`LedgerRow::relied()`, on every build) `pass`, or `absent` on `browser-tools-prompt` alone: a seventeen-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row reads unverified (`cli_verified:false`) until the next `viola verify`, and so does an eighteen-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, a twenty-one-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, a twenty-two-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board , a twenty-three-row stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row or a twenty-two-row stamp written before chunk 2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row; a stamp's `rows` maps each row id to `pass` or `fail`, browser-tools-prompt may also read `absent`, and trust-record holds the trust writer's code word instead when no record was written

- `cargo test --workspace --doc` — doctests (nextest cannot run them); otherwise nextest is the runner: a plain `cargo test` run (`cargo test --bin viola`) is not supported, and under it root-bin cases are known-cause reds (test-plan §2 Runner)

- `bash scripts/lint-probes.sh`: proves every clippy ban fires and every control passes, plus the fail-closed raw-`event!` grep (its last line counts the bans fired and the controls clean; CI runs it on the Linux lint leg).

- `bash scripts/orphans-check.sh [--probe]` — `cargo modules orphans --deny` per lib/bin target (last line `orphans-check: N/N targets clean`; the probe's last line counts its planted orphans fired and its control clean); CI job `lint` on `ubuntu-latest`
- `cargo modules dependencies --package <crate> --lib` — the on-demand boundary review only: `--acyclic` is not a gate (cargo-modules reads every type ↔ inherent method as a cycle)

- `bash scripts/deny-probes.sh` — proves every ban fires (its last line counts every probe banned and the control clean: each ban one probe (the serde_json `unbounded_depth` ban's row `serde_json-unbounded-depth` among them), plus probe `channel-tokio-edge` for the `channel-tokio-free.sh` tree form with its channel control; needs the network)

- Steps in order: `cargo build --workspace --features viola/fake-agent` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/harness` (the CLI's `<bin dir>` is `target/harness/debug`) → a not-yet-existing home under `target/e2e-home/viola-session-*/home` (the base first prepared by `Workspace::ensure_e2e_home`: a plain directory is created; a link, as on the Linux dev host, must point at an absolute, real, owner-only directory, made again 0700 when it is gone, and refused when its filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), else `build-failed`) → copy the fake agent to `target/agent-run/<session>/bin/claude` on a harness-scoped `PATH` (per child via `Command::env`) → `viola verify --home` under a test-owned user home (its config file seeded empty and owner-only, the fake agent told that config file by `--trust-config`) against it with `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root <workspace root> --dialogs --framing`, the fake agent given `--transcript` beside `--framing` (without it Run B's echo probe is skipped and the `local-command-echo` row fails) (print probe + all six interactive runs, Run B with its added pastes (the long, tag-like and newline texts, then `/compact`, then `/clear`), its one `claude agents --json` read and, on Unix, its one probe `--settings`, and Run E, the `--resume` start of Run B's first session; every relied row, `LedgerRow::relied()`) unless `--unstamped` → the `--agents-mode recorded|oversize|malformed` value (default `recorded`; a stale file removed before verify) written to the `agents-mode` file beside `bin/claude`, after verify because Run B reads `claude agents --json` through that copy, and recorded as `agents_mode` in `session.json` and `supervise.json` → `viola-harness supervise` as an ordinary child (outlives `boot`; the agent-run CLI's boot leaves it untied, stopping only via `stop.request`; it hands the fake agent `--screens --trusted-root <cwd>`; the supervised wrappers of a stamped session run under a session user home seeded with an empty config) owning one portable-pty outer PTY per instance via `viola-pty` (master writer kept until the child exits, one drain thread per master).

- Answers `--version` like the real CLI. Standing as `hyprctl` by its own file name (in a test-scoped bin dir, in place of the real `hyprctl`; viola-hyprland's own unit tests serve `hyprctl` by a planted shell stub instead, because cargo-mutants runs only the mutated package's tests, so a root-package test cannot kill that crate's mutants), it reads its mode and reply set from files beside its exe, never from the env. It reads hook commands from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (the `--plugin-dir` `run` passes). Only an absolute exec-form `command` is spawned: no shell, no PATH; a group's `matcher` is evaluated against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name` (`hook_commands(…, tool)`). A non-absolute command is receipted `command_absolute:false, ran:false` and never run. The payload is `<fixtures>/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json`, with only `prompt` set for UserPromptSubmit and the fixture's trailing newline kept, so the recorded prompt yields the recorded bytes; under `--resume <id>` the launch SessionStart is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it, else its recorded `SessionStart.default` (a set without the variant), with `source` `resume` and `session_id` the id given (with `--fork-session`, the compiled fork id), and no other payload is built save the compact replay's `SessionStart.compact-1` under `--framing`, whose `session_id` is set to the last SessionStart the agent fired, and under `--transcript` the launch SessionStart's `transcript_path`.

- Root fixture chain: `tests/support/` (`home` → `fake_agent_path` → `stamped_home`, a copy, never a link, of one `viola verify` stamp per build (taken against the fake agent at the recorded `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` over `fixtures/claude` under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only, the fake agent told that config file (a `--record` verify keeps the real HOME and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead), the fake agent given `--transcript` beside `--framing`, once per pair of built binaries, under an exclusive lock, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes) → `booted_wrapper`; `StampedHome::unstamped` for the unverified path; every long-lived viola child a root test spawns is tied to its spawning test thread by a parent-death kill (spawned only on a thread that outlives it; exiting when its recorded parent is already gone; `cross_killed_test_census_finds_no_untied_viola_spawn` finds no untied viola spawn in any test source; `every_test_verify_runs_under_a_test_home` holds every test-started `viola verify` start tied to a test-owned home, and every test-started `viola run` and `viola revive` runs under a test-owned user home, never the runner's real HOME, with a closed exempt list whose every entry carries its reason, proven red on a planted untied start), so a killed or panicked test leaves no wrapper or fake agent, and a Drop guard that kills, then waits, still covers the normal end; `Wrapper::stop` waits for the endpoint to be unconnectable, not only the exit; `wait_ready` at its deadline appends the stalled wrapper's state — its last `run-<name>.ndjson` event, its `/proc/<pid>/wchan` and the `stat` state field (`note_stall`) — to the watch report before the panic, signalling nothing and adding nothing to a passing boot).
